findings.problem: A caller could submit the externally modified current SHA and bypass the persisted editor session SHA.
findings.rootCause: The current-file check chose caller baseSha instead of independently checking both session and caller bases.
findings.fix: Require disk SHA to equal session SHA and caller base SHA to equal session SHA; added external-drift regression.

findings.problem: Journal append could succeed before session persistence, leaving timeline journal and stacks inconsistent if session write failed.
findings.rootCause: The mutation was atomic per file but not compensating across the three state files.
findings.fix: Append records are fsynced without rewriting prior history; partial writes and session-write failures truncate to the prior byte offset while Timeline rollback restores the before snapshot.

findings.problem: Empty commands and duplicate caller-supplied command IDs could create ambiguous or no-op history.
findings.rootCause: The JSON schema constraints were not duplicated at the runtime trust boundary.
findings.fix: Runtime rejects empty changes and command IDs already present in the digest-validated journal.

findings.problem: SFX projection always exposed timeTick even when the source contract used targetLandingTick, and omitted the Inspector value.
findings.rootCause: The display field was hard-coded instead of following the chosen timing reference.
findings.fix: Projection now exposes and populates the real tick field dynamically; regression asserts the mapping.

findings.problem: Sanitized source IDs could collide and make item selection target the wrong Timeline object.
findings.rootCause: Stable IDs were generated but uniqueness was not enforced.
findings.fix: Projection rejects duplicate item IDs and requires unique source IDs.

findings.problem: Browser editor sessions were expired only during a later open and could otherwise live beyond twelve hours.
findings.rootCause: Expiry cleanup and session lookup were separate paths.
findings.fix: All editor media and mutation requests now resolve through one expiry-enforcing session lookup.

findings.problem: Initial hidden workspace state, missing favicon and narrow-screen panel headings produced misleading or broken presentation.
findings.rootCause: Hidden-state CSS and small-screen heading constraints were missing.
findings.fix: Added authoritative hidden styling, data favicon, responsive heading wrapping and verified desktop/mobile screenshots with zero console errors.

findings.problem: The preview provider runtime trusted purpose and several registry field shapes when called outside the CLI wrapper.
findings.rootCause: Validation was split between CLI argument handling and the provider module.
findings.fix: The module now rejects unknown purposes, malformed provider contracts and final providers missing the complete canonical capability set.

findings.problem: Studio stored a bare file identity while the range server required {path, identity}, so a real source video request failed although missing-source API tests passed.
findings.rootCause: The integration test never exercised /api/editor/media with an existing source file.
findings.fix: Bind source media as the server contract shape and add an identity-checked HTTP byte-range regression.

findings.problem: The plan promised snapshot recovery, but history only recommended recovery; a truncated final record followed by a newline was not even recognized as a recoverable tail.
findings.rootCause: Recovery reporting and recovery execution were conflated, and truncation compared against the raw split-line index.
findings.fix: Add explicit expected-SHA recover and reopen commands, archive prior state, restore only the last verified snapshot, re-chain history, and parse the last non-empty journal line.

findings.problem: Inverse capture for JSON array add replaced an existing element or tried to remove the '-' pseudo-index, so undo could leave shifted or extra entries.
findings.rootCause: Object-add inversion rules were reused for array insertion and append.
findings.fix: Resolve parent type and concrete append index before mutation; array add always inverts to remove the inserted index, with focused regressions.

findings.problem: Timeline sessions used path.resolve rather than realpath and runtime command validation accepted numeric strings, unknown fields and inherited property names.
findings.rootCause: The documented schema was not fully enforced at the kernel boundary and symlink identity was not canonicalized.
findings.fix: Bind projection/journal/session to fs.realpath, reject extra/control/oversized fields and non-number changes, use own-property allowlists, and require visual edit ticks on frame boundaries.

findings.problem: The browser playhead treated output time as raw source time, producing the wrong frame after cuts or reordering; CLI projection also hashed the full source on every new process.
findings.rootCause: Approximate preview lacked an EDL-to-source mapping and projection mixed interactive identity with final content hashing.
findings.fix: Map output ticks through picture segments, disclose single-picture overlap behavior, and use fast source identity by default while retaining opt-in source hashing.

findings.problem: FFmpeg was declared final-eligible without confirming that the current runtime existed.
findings.rootCause: Registry availability represented implementation state but was read as runtime state.
findings.fix: Require and expose a current ffmpeg -version runtime probe before final eligibility succeeds.

decision: All fourteen producer-review findings are fixed and verified by focused regression, 159-test full regression, real-browser EDL/apply/undo/redo journeys, static/privacy checks, installer regression and dual-agent install readback. Independent final review remains a separate completion boundary.
